articles.title: ‘Like Saddam opened a Cheesecake Factory’: how did the restaurant end up in a Maga fight over ‘elitism’?
articles.summary: Obama has been accused of ‘snobbery’ over his Trump diss, as people rush to defend the restaurant chain’s ‘affordable opulence’ Around lunchtime on Tuesday, a Rolls-Royce stopped at the intersection of Beverly Drive and Dayton Way in Beverly Hills, California.
body: Up the street, across from the upmarket Erewhon grocery store – home to $21 smoothies – a few diners sat outside an American landmark: the Cheesecake Factory.
The beloved restaurant chain began here in Beverly Hills in 1978; now it has hundreds of locations across the US and Canada. And this week, it’s become the US’s latest surreal culture-war touchstone.

It started when Barack Obama, campaigning for Democrats in Ohio, made a joke that hit Donald Trump right in the real estate. Referring to his successor’s remodeling obsession, the former president said: “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. Just gold everywhere.”

The joke was about maximalism: Saddam had 100 palaces and loved gold plating, and the Cheesecake Factory, while affordable for many, offers swanky surroundings that a curmudgeon might describe as over the top. While the Beverly Hills restaurant has a fairly staid interior, a nearby location at Los Angeles’s Grove mall has a grand staircase, floral paintings on the ceilings and an ornate balcony.

articles.title: How to turn excess custard into a fruity treat – recipe
articles.summary: A fool is absurdly simple – just fruit stirred through custard or yoghurt with. maybe a bit of cream – and you can then add whatever bits and bobs you fancy from the fridge.
body: Fool is one of my go-to desserts for two reasons: first, its pure simplicity – it’s little more than custard or yoghurt mixed with whipped cream and pureed fruit – and, second, its adaptability to the seasons. Gooseberry, rhubarb and strawberry are traditionally the most foolish fruits, but just about any fruit goes. British blackberries are still available and apples are in their prime right now, so I’ve gone for those, but use whatever you’ve got in store.

I usually make fool with yoghurt, not least because it’s much less work than making custard from scratch, but I’ve got lots of leftover custard from this week’s Food Filter taste test, so I’m going for a custard base here. I’m always looking for ways to use up small amounts of bits and pieces in the fridge, such as the end of a pot of custard or yoghurt, then add a few other ingredients to elevate remnants into regalia.

articles.title: 9 Best Hotels in Rio de Janeiro for a Taste of the Carioca Lifestyle
articles.summary: From grand hotels on Copacabana to intimate retreats in Santa Teresa, these stays capture Rio’s singular mix of beach life, Brazilian design, and warm hospitality.
body: “I live where you vacation” takes on a whole other meaning when, like me, you're based in Rio de Janeiro. I live smack in the middle of South America ’s two hottest beaches—Copacabana and Ipanema—but it’s not the ocean that keeps me in Brazil's buzziest city. It’s the life that happens around it. It’s the sound of the first coconuts being cut open on the beach in the early morning, the sight of barefoot surfers passing beneath my window, and the honey-like melody of bossa nova flowing from a nearby beach kiosk. Not everyone can live here, of course. But luckily, the best hotels in Rio de Janeiro give you a good taste of what it feels like to be a local in Brazil’s most exciting metropolis.

articles.title: A Dermatologist’s Guide to Sunscreen in Winter
articles.summary: Do you need sunscreen in winter? While it might seem unnecessary, experts say wearing a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or more is non-negotiable to stave off sun rays.
body: Sunscreen in winter might seem a little over-the-top, even for those among us who take their skin care very seriously. But it’s not just that sunscreen itself is important—which it very much is, no matter the season. After all, sunlight is still sunlight, whatever the season. “If you’re outdoors and can see your hand in front of your face, there is enough UV exposure to cause skin damage,” says Mona Gohara, MD, a board-certified dermatologist in New Haven, Connecticut. And on top of that, she adds, snow can act like a giant reflector, bouncing up to 80% of UVA and UVB rays back onto your skin.

And, even if you’re spending more time indoors, you don’t get a free pass. In fact, skipping the sunscreen can still cause issues, since “visible light and blue light from laptops, phones, and LED bulbs continue to hit the skin,” says Dr. Gohara. “This is particularly important for women of color and those with melasma, because visible light significantly drives pigment production.” And certain sunscreen formulas —namely, tinted ones—deliver added protection against this type of light damage.
points: While it might seem unnecessary, experts say wearing a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or more is non-negotiable to stave off sun rays.

articles.title: The 38 Best Restaurants in Barcelona, According to a Local Food Guide
articles.summary: From Barcelona’s towering churches and bustling avenues to the sun-drenched beaches and idyllic plazas, it’s obvious why this city captures visitors’ hearts. You can also eat incredibly well here, and often for not very much money — though Barcelona loves a tasting menu and the World’s 50 Best…
body: Start with some classic tapas and paella (both great but neither entirely Catalan) and be sure to seek out local gems like bittersweet vermouth, seasonal seafood, and homestyle Catalan cuisine. But after writing and revising this list for nearly a decade, I have to insist you don’t overlook the city’s burgeoning global cuisines; save room for Calabrese paninis, Northeast Asian sharing plates with natural wines, towering fried chicken sandwiches, South Indian fish stews, and nose-to-tail yakitori.

We update this list quarterly to make sure it reflects the ever-changing Barcelona dining scene. Our write-ups include insider tips from our experienced writers and editors, as well as a rough range of pricing for each destination — ranging from $ for quick, inexpensive meals with dishes largely under $10 (or the equivalent in euros), to $$$$ for places where entrees exceed $30.

New to the map in October 2026: Lluritu, a Mediterranean marisquería with three locations across the city; a parallel universe of Catalan culinary history in a former water bottling plant at Franca; and the trendy modern Catalan cuisine of Manda Huevos.

articles.title: Meet ‘Wheat Meat,’ the Best Plant-Based Protein
articles.summary: Seitan is the ultimate plant-based protein, especially if you’re trying to eat less meat or stick to a vegetarian or vegan diet. Here, experts break down everything you need to know.
body: If you’re trying to eat less meat or go fully plant-based, finding a protein-rich meat alternative for meals becomes a top priority. You can turn to the usual suspects—tempeh, legumes, and nuts—or take the road less traveled with unexpected protein sources like seaweed. But one plant-based option may be better than the rest, and people often forget it’s super protein rich. Have you heard of seitan?

As Real Nutrition founder Amy Shapiro, RD, explains, seitan is a plant-based food made from wheat gluten, the main protein source found in wheat. It’s been used for centuries in Asian cuisines, Shapiro says, and is now one of the more sought-after protein sources, especially for those who don’t want to eat animal products.

“You can think of it as wheat meat,” adds sports dietitian Roxana Ehsani, MS, RD. “It can mimic the texture of chicken, and because its flavor is fairly neutral, it takes on the flavor of whatever you season it with. It’s a great protein substitute for anyone following a vegan or vegetarian diet.”
points: Seitan is the ultimate plant-based protein, especially if you’re trying to eat less meat or stick to a vegetarian or vegan diet.

articles.title: Digestive Walking Helps with Bloating and Blood Sugar
articles.summary: Naturopath Julie Coignet talks about the heath benefits of digestive walking after a meal.
body: Going for a stroll after dinner isn’t just a nice part of a nighttime routine. The habit of going for a walk after any meal —breakfast, lunch, or dinner—is actually one of the most effective ways to aid in digestion.

“Walking affects two mechanisms at the same time,” explains naturopath Julie Coignet. First, gastric motility: “The gentle movement of the body mechanically stimulates the progression of food through the stomach and intestines, which speeds up gastric emptying and limits fermentation time”—and thus reduces gas and bloating.

Second, blood sugar levels: “Walking right after eating engages the muscles, which absorb some of the blood glucose directly, without waiting for insulin.” It’s a double benefit—for digestion and for afternoon energy. “It’s no coincidence that our grandparents used to take a short digestive walk after a meal without even thinking about it,” Coignet points out. “It was a common-sense habit long before it became a scientific recommendation. We’ve just lost that along the way.”

articles.title: This Very Southern Cornbread Recipe Is a Winner Every Time
articles.summary: When I was growing up in a Southern household, we ate cornbread often. It was a must with red beans and rice, a simple roasted chicken and rice dinner, and, of course, on New Year’s Day with black-eyed peas and collard greens for good luck. Making the cornbread usually fell to me and my sisters.
body: In my book, a good cornbread should always be made in a cast iron skillet. That helps yield a golden-brown crust and a pillowy-soft interior. Start by melting the butter in the skillet first, then pour the batter in and slide the whole thing in the oven — the result is a perfect, buttery, crisp crust with a beautiful golden color. But inside the cornbread is soft and tender, with a more savory than sweet flavor (no sugar added here!). The addition of both buttermilk and vinegar helps keep the crumb moist while also giving it a bit of a tang. It’s also nice and fluffy, thanks to the baking powder and baking soda.
